text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek continued coalition talks on Wednesday, but no agreement with the rightist parties, which hold 44 out of 90 parliamentary seats, has been reached yet.

- The State Council (upper house of parliament) proposed that council members should be elected directly, as happened in the first council election in 1992. The next election is due at the end of 1997.
- Slovenia's largest bank state-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka said its balance sheet assets rose 14 percent to 490 billion tolars ($3.2 billion) in 1996.
- A three-day meeting of CEFTA members including Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Poland, Slovakia and Hungary, on liberalising trade in agricultural products started in Ljubljana on Wednesday.

- Some 32 percent of Slovenians believe early elections are the best solution to the current parliamentary deadlock, after the November general election gave an even number of votes to rightist and leftist parties, an opinion poll showed.

- The association of employers said a social agreement, by which the growth of salaries should be two percentage points lower than the growth of GDP, was not fulfilled in 1996 as the growth of salaries last year exceeded 3.5 percent, while GDP rose 3.9 percent.
